verses.text: Concerning di children of Ammon. Di Lord talk like dis: “Israel no get sons? E no get heir? Why den Milcom dey possess Gad, and im people dwell for im cities?

Therefore see, di days dey come,” talk di Lord, “wey I go cause di alarm of war to dey heard against Rabbah of di children of Ammon. E go become desolate heap, and im daughters go dey burned with fire. Den Israel go possess dem wey possess am,” talk di Lord.

“Howl, Heshbon, because Ai dey laid waste! Cry, una daughters of Rabbah! Gird una with sackcloth. Lament, and run to and fro among di fences, because Milcom go go into captivity, im priests and im princes together.
Why you boast for di valleys, your flowing valley, backsliding daughter? Dem wey trust for her treasures, saying, ‘Who go come against me?’
See, I go bring terror on you,” talk di Lord, di Lord of Armies, “from all wey dey round about you. Una go dey driven out everyone straight before am, and nobody go gather up di fugitives.
But afterward I go bring again di captivity of di children of Ammon,” talk di Lord.
Concerning Edom. Di Lord of Armies talk like dis: “Wisdom no dey again for Teman? Counsel don perish from di prudent? Dem wisdom don vanish?
Flee, turn back, dwell deep, una inhabitants of Dedan, because I go bring di calamity of Esau on am, di time wey I go visit am.
If grape gatherers come to you, dem no go leave some gleaning grapes? If thieves for night, dem go destroy until dem don enough.
But I don strip Esau bare. I don uncover im secret places, and e no go fit hide imself. Im offspring dey destroyed, and im brothers, and im neighbours, and e no dey again.
Leave your fatherless children. I go preserve dem alive. Make your widows trust for me.”
Because di Lord talk like dis: “See, dem wey no suppose drink di cup go surely drink am. You be im wey go altogether go unpunished? You no go go unpunished, but you go surely drink.
Because I don swear by myself,” talk di Lord, “say Bozrah go become desolation, reproach, waste, and curse. All im cities go be perpetual wastes.”
I don hear message from di Lord, and ambassador dey sent among di nations, saying, “Gather una yourselves together, and come against her, and rise up to di battle!
Because see, I don make you small among di nations, and despised among men.

Di terror wey you dey bring, di pride of your heart, don deceive you, you wey dwell for di clefts of di rock, wey hold di height of di hill. Though you make your nest as high as di eagle, I go bring you down from dere,” talk di Lord.
“Edom go become astonishment. Everyone wey pass by am go dey astonished, and go hiss because of all im plagues.
As for di overthrow of Sodom and Gomorrah and di neighbouring cities of dem,” talk di Lord, “no man go dwell dere, neither any son of man go sojourn inside am.

See, e go come up like lion from di thickets of di Jordan against di strong habitation, because I go suddenly make am run away from am. Who be di chosen man wey I go appoint over am? Because who dey like me? Who go appoint me time? Who be di shepherd wey fit stand before me?”

Therefore hear di counsel of di Lord, wey e don take against Edom, and im purposes, wey e don purpose against di inhabitants of Teman: Surely dem go drag dem away, even di little ones of di flock. Surely e go make dem habitation desolate over dem.
Di earth tremble at di noise of dem fall. Di cry, im noise dey heard for di Red Sea.
See, e go come up and fly as di eagle, and spread im wings against Bozrah. Di heart of di mighty men of Edom for dat day go be like di heart of woman for her labour pains.
Concerning Damascus: Hamath dey confounded, and Arpad, because dem don hear evil news. Dem dey melted away. Sorrow dey for di sea. E no fit dey quiet.
Damascus don become feeble. E turn imself to flee, and trembling don seize am. Anguish and sorrows don take hold of am, like woman for labour.
How di city of praise no dey left, di city of my joy?
“Therefore her young men go fall for her streets, and all di men of war go dey brought to silence for dat day,” talk di Lord of Armies.
“I go kindle fire for di wall of Damascus, and e go devour di palaces of Ben Hadad.”
Concerning Kedar, and concerning di kingdoms of Hazor, wey Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon strike. Di Lord talk like dis: “Arise, go up to Kedar, and destroy di children of di east.
Dem go take dem tents and dem flocks. Dem go take for demselves dem curtains, and all dem vessels, and dem camels. Dem go cry to dem, ‘Terror on every side!’
Flee, wander far off, dwell deep, una inhabitants of Hazor,” talk di Lord, “because Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon don take counsel against una, and don conceive purpose against una.
Arise, go up to di nation wey dey at ease, wey dwell securely,” talk di Lord, “wey no get gates nor bars, wey dwell alone.

Dem camels go be for plunder, and di multitude of dem livestock for spoil. I go scatter to all winds dem wey cut di corners of dem hair, and I go bring dem calamity from every side of am,” talk di Lord.
“Hazor go be habitation of jackals, desolation forever. No man go dwell dere, neither any son of man sojourn inside am.”
Di word of di Lord wey come to Jeremiah di prophet against Elam, for di beginning of di reign of Zedekiah king of Judah, say,
“Di Lord of Armies talk like dis: See, I go break di bow of Elam, di chief of dem might.
I go bring on Elam di four winds from di four ends of heaven, and go scatter dem toward all dose winds. No nation go dey where di outcasts of Elam no go come.
I go cause Elam dey dismayed before dem enemies, and before dem wey seek dem life. I go bring evil on dem, even my fierce anger,” talk di Lord. “I go send di sword after dem, until I don consume dem.
I go set my throne for Elam, and go destroy from dere king and princes,” talk di Lord.
“But e go happen for di latter days say I go cause di captivity of Elam to return,” talk di Lord.
Di word wey di Lord speak concerning Babylon, concerning di land of di Chaldeans, by Jeremiah di prophet.
“Declare among di nations and publish, and set up banner. Publish, and no hide. Talk, ‘Babylon dey taken. Bel dey disgraced. Merodach dey dismayed. Her images dey disgraced. Her idols dey dismayed.’
Because out of di north, nation don come up against her. E go make her land desolate, and no one go dwell inside am. Both man and animal don flee. Dem don go.
For dose days, and for dat time,” talk di Lord, “di children of Israel go come, dem and di children of Judah together. Dem go go on dem way weeping, and go seek di Lord dem God.
Dem go ask di way to Zion, with dem faces toward am, saying, ‘Come, make we join ourselves to di Lord for everlasting covenant wey no go dey forgotten.’
My people don be lost sheep. Dem shepherds don cause dem to go astray. Dem don turn dem away on di mountains. Dem don go from mountain to hill. Dem don forget dem resting place.
All wey find dem don devour dem. Dem adversaries talk, ‘We no offend, because dem don sin against di Lord, di habitation of righteousness, even di Lord, di hope of dem fathers.’
Flee out of di middle of Babylon, and go out of di land of di Chaldeans, and be like di male goats before di flocks.

Because see, I go stir up and cause to come up against Babylon assembly of great nations from di north country. Dem go set dem in array against her. From dere she go dey taken. Dem arrows na like skilful mighty man wey no go return in vain.
Chaldea go be plunder. All wey plunder her go dey satisfied,” talk di Lord.
“Because una dey glad, because una rejoice, una wey plunder my heritage, because una dey frisky like heifer wey dey thresh, and neigh like strong horses,
una mother go dey greatly ashamed. She wey bear una go dey confounded. See, di last of di nations go be wilderness, dry land, and desert.
Because of di wrath of di Lord e no go dey inhabited, but e go be wholly desolate. Everyone wey go by Babylon go dey astonished, and hiss at all her plagues.
Set una yourselves in array against Babylon round about, all una wey bend di bow. Shoot at her. Spare no arrows, because she don sin against di Lord.
Shout against her round about. She don give her hand. Her bulwarks don fall. Her walls dey thrown down, because na di vengeance of di Lord. Take vengeance on her. As she don do, do to her.
Cut off di sower from Babylon, and im wey handle di sickle for di time of harvest. For fear of di oppressing sword everyone go turn to im own people, and everyone go flee to im own land.
Israel na scattered sheep. Di lions don drive am away. First di king of Assyria devour am, and now at last Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon don break im bones.”
Therefore di Lord of Armies, di God of Israel, talk like dis: “See, I go punish di king of Babylon and im land, as I don punish di king of Assyria.
I go bring Israel again to im pasture, and e go feed on Carmel and Bashan. Im soul go dey satisfied for di hills of Ephraim and Gilead.
For dose days, and for dat time,” talk di Lord, “dem go seek for di iniquity of Israel, and e no go dey, and di sins of Judah, and dem no go dey found, because I go pardon dem wey I leave as remnant.
Go up against di land of Merathaim, even against am, and against di inhabitants of Pekod. Kill and utterly destroy after dem,” talk di Lord, “and do according to all wey I don command you.”
Di sound of battle dey for di land, and of great destruction.
How di hammer of di whole earth dey cut apart and broken! How Babylon don become desolation among di nations!
I don lay snare for you, and you dey taken, Babylon, and you no know am. You dey found, and also caught, because you don contend against di Lord.
Di Lord don open im armoury, and don bring out di weapons of im indignation, because dis na work of di Lord, di Lord of Armies, for di land of di Chaldeans.
Come against her from di utmost border. Open her storehouses. Cast her up like heaps, and destroy her utterly. Make nothing of her remain.
Kill all her bulls. Make dem go down to di slaughter. Woe to dem, because dem day don come, di time of dem visitation.
Di voice of dem wey flee and escape out of di land of Babylon, to declare for Zion di vengeance of di Lord our God, di vengeance of im temple.

Call together archers against Babylon, all wey bend di bow. Encamp against her round about. Make none of her escape. Recompense her according to her work. According to all wey she don do, do to her, because she don dey proud against di Lord, against di Holy One of Israel.
“Therefore her young men go fall for di streets, and all her men of war go dey brought to silence for dat day,” talk di Lord.
“See, I dey against you, you proud one,” talk di Lord, di Lord of Armies, “because your day don come, di time wey I go visit you.
Di proud one go stumble and fall, and nobody go raise am up. I go kindle fire for im cities, and e go devour all wey dey round am.”
Di Lord of Armies talk like dis: “Di children of Israel and di children of Judah dey oppressed together. All wey take dem captive hold dem fast. Dem refuse to let dem go.
Dem Redeemer dey strong. Di Lord of Armies na im name. E go thoroughly plead dem cause, so that e go give rest to di earth, and disquiet di inhabitants of Babylon.
Sword dey on di Chaldeans,” talk di Lord, “and on di inhabitants of Babylon, and on her princes, and on her wise men.
Sword dey on di boasters, and dem go become fools. Sword dey on her mighty men, and dem go dey dismayed.
Sword dey on dem horses, and on dem chariots, and on all di mixed people wey dey inside her, and dem go become women. Sword dey on her treasures, and dem go dey robbed.
Drought dey on her waters, and dem go dey dried up, because na land of engraved images, and dem dey mad over idols.

Therefore di wild animals of di desert with di wolves go dwell dere, and di ostriches go dwell inside am. E no go dey inhabited any more forever, neither e go dey dwelt in from generation to generation.
As when God overthrow Sodom and Gomorrah and di neighbouring cities of dem,” talk di Lord, “so no man go dwell dere, neither any son of man sojourn inside am.
See, people dey come from di north. Great nation and many kings go dey stirred up from di uttermost parts of di earth.
Dem lay hold on bow and spear. Dem dey cruel, and no mercy dey for dem. Dem voice roar like di sea, and dem ride on horses, everyone set in array, as man for battle, against you, daughter of Babylon.
Di king of Babylon don hear di report of dem, and im hands hang limp. Anguish don take hold of am, and pain as of woman for labour.

See, e go come up like lion from di thickets of di Jordan against di strong habitation, because I go suddenly make dem run away from am. Who be di chosen man wey I go appoint over am? Because who dey like me? Who go appoint me time? Who be di shepherd wey fit stand before me?

Therefore hear di counsel of di Lord, wey e don take against Babylon, and im purposes, wey e don purpose against di land of di Chaldeans: Surely dem go drag dem away, even di little ones of di flock. Surely e go make dem habitation desolate over dem.
Di earth tremble at di noise of di taking of Babylon, and di cry dey heard among di nations.”
Di Lord talk like dis: “See, I go stir up against Babylon, and against dem wey dwell for Leb Kamai, destroying wind.
I go send to Babylon strangers, and dem go winnow her. Dem go empty her land, because for di day of trouble dem go dey against her round about.
Make di archer bend im bow against am wey bend, and against am wey lift imself up for im coat of mail. No spare her young men. Utterly destroy all her army.
Dem go fall down slain for di land of di Chaldeans, and thrust through for her streets.
Because Israel no dey forsaken, nor Judah, by im God, di Lord of Armies, though dem land dey full of guilt against di Holy One of Israel.
Flee out of di middle of Babylon, and save every man im life. No dey cut off for her iniquity, because na time of di Lord vengeance. E go render to her recompense.
Babylon don be golden cup for di Lord hand, wey make all di earth drunk. Di nations don drink of her wine. Therefore di nations dey mad.
Babylon don suddenly fall and dey destroyed. Wail for her. Take balm for her pain. Maybe she go dey healed.
We for don heal Babylon, but she no dey healed. Forsake her, and make we go everyone to im own country, because her judgment reach to heaven, and dey lifted up even to di skies.
Di Lord don bring forth our righteousness. Come, and make we declare for Zion di work of di Lord our God.

Make di arrows sharp. Hold di shields. Di Lord don stir up di spirit of di kings of di Medes, because im purpose dey against Babylon, to destroy am, because na di vengeance of di Lord, di vengeance of im temple.
Set up banner against di walls of Babylon. Make di watch strong. Set di watchmen. Prepare di ambushes, because di Lord don both purpose and do wetin e speak against di inhabitants of Babylon.
You wey dwell on many waters, rich in treasures, your end don come, di measure of your covetousness.
Di Lord of Armies don swear by imself, saying, ‘Surely I go fill you with men, as with locusts, and dem go lift up shout against you.’
Na im make di earth by im power, wey establish di world by im wisdom, and by im understanding don stretch out di heavens.
When e utter im voice, tumult of waters dey for di heavens, and e cause di clouds to ascend from di ends of di earth. E make lightnings with di rain, and bring out di wind from im storehouses.
Every man dey brutish, without knowledge. Every goldsmith dey disgraced by im engraved image, because im molten image na falsehood, and no breath dey inside dem.
Dem na vanity, work of delusion. For di time of dem visitation dem go perish.
Di Portion of Jacob no be like dem, because e na di Maker of all things, and Israel na di tribe of im inheritance. Di Lord of Armies na im name.”
“You na my battle axe and weapons of war. With you I go break nations in pieces. With you I go destroy kingdoms.
With you I go break in pieces di horse and im rider. With you I go break in pieces di chariot and im rider.
With you I go break in pieces man and woman. With you I go break in pieces old man and youth. With you I go break in pieces young man and maiden.
With you I go break in pieces di shepherd and im flock. With you I go break in pieces di farmer and im team. With you I go break in pieces governors and rulers.
I go render to Babylon and to all di inhabitants of Chaldea all dem evil wey dem don do for Zion for una sight,” talk di Lord.
“See, I dey against you, destroying mountain,” talk di Lord, “wey destroy all di earth. I go stretch out my hand on you, and roll you down from di rocks, and go make you burnt mountain.
Dem no go take from you stone for cornerstone, nor stone for foundations, but you go be desolate forever,” talk di Lord.

Set up banner for di land. Blow di trumpet among di nations. Prepare di nations against her. Call together against her di kingdoms of Ararat, Minni, and Ashkenaz. Appoint captain against her. Cause di horses to come up like swarming locusts.
Prepare against her di nations, di kings of di Medes, dem governors, and all dem rulers, and all di land of dem dominion.
Di land tremble and dey in pain, because di purposes of di Lord dey established against Babylon, to make di land of Babylon desolation without inhabitant.
Di mighty men of Babylon don stop fighting. Dem remain for di strongholds. Dem might don fail. Dem don become like women. Dem dwellings dey set on fire. Dem bars dey broken.
One runner go run to meet another, and one messenger to meet another, to show di king of Babylon say im city dey taken from end to end,
and di fords dey seized, and di reeds dey burned with fire, and di men of war dey frightened.
Because di Lord of Armies, di God of Israel, talk like dis: “Di daughter of Babylon be like threshing floor for di time wey dem tread am. Yet small while, and di time of harvest go come for her.”
“Nebuchadnezzar di king of Babylon don devour me. E don crush me. E don make me empty vessel. E don swallow me up like dragon. E don fill im belly with my delicacies. E don cast me out.”
“Make di violence wey dem do to me and to my flesh dey on Babylon,” di inhabitant of Zion go talk. “Make my blood dey on di inhabitants of Chaldea,” Jerusalem go talk.
Therefore di Lord talk like dis: “See, I go plead your cause, and take vengeance for you. I go dry up her sea, and make her fountain dry.
Babylon go become heaps, dwelling place for jackals, astonishment, and hissing, without inhabitant.
Dem go roar together like young lions. Dem go growl like lions cubs.
For dem heat I go prepare dem feast, and I go make dem drunk, so that dem go rejoice, and sleep perpetual sleep, and no wake,” talk di Lord.
“I go bring dem down like lambs to di slaughter, like rams with male goats.
How Sheshach dey taken! And di praise of di whole earth dey seized! How Babylon don become astonishment among di nations!
Di sea don come up on Babylon. E dey covered with di multitude of im waves.
Her cities don become desolation, dry land, and desert, land wey no man dwell inside, neither any son of man pass through.
I go punish Bel for Babylon, and I go bring out of im mouth wetin e don swallow. Di nations no go flow to am any more. Yes, di wall of Babylon don fall.
My people, go out of di middle of her, and save every man im life from di fierce anger of di Lord.

Make your heart no faint, neither una fear di rumour wey go dey heard for di land. Because rumour go come one year, and after dat for another year rumour, and violence for di land, ruler against ruler.
Therefore see, di days dey come, wey I go execute judgment on di engraved images of Babylon. Her whole land go dey confounded, and all her slain go fall for di middle of her.
Den di heavens and di earth, and all wey dey inside dem, go sing for joy over Babylon, because di destroyers go come to her from di north,” talk di Lord.
“As Babylon don cause di slain of Israel to fall, so for Babylon go fall di slain of all di earth.
Una wey don escape di sword, go, no stand still. Remember di Lord from far, and make Jerusalem come into una mind.
We dey ashamed, because we don hear reproach. Shame don cover our faces, because strangers don come into di sanctuaries of di Lord house.
Therefore see, di days dey come,” talk di Lord, “wey I go execute judgment on her engraved images, and through all her land di wounded go groan.
Though Babylon mount up to heaven, and though she fortify di height of her strength, yet destroyers go come from me to her,” talk di Lord.
Di sound of cry from Babylon, and great destruction from di land of di Chaldeans!
Because di Lord dey destroy Babylon, and destroy out of her di great voice. Dem waves roar like great waters. Di noise of dem voice dey uttered.
Because di destroyer don come on her, even on Babylon, and her mighty men dey taken. Dem bows dey broken in pieces, because di Lord na God of recompense. E go surely repay.
“I go make her princes and her wise men drunk, her governors and her deputies, and her mighty men. Dem go sleep perpetual sleep, and no wake,” talk di King, wey im name na di Lord of Armies.

Di Lord of Armies talk like dis: “Di broad walls of Babylon go dey utterly overthrown, and her high gates go dey burned with fire. Di peoples go labour for vanity, and di nations for di fire. Dem go dey weary.”
Di word wey Jeremiah di prophet command Seraiah, Neriah pikin, Maaseiah pikin, when e go with Zedekiah king of Judah to Babylon for di fourth year of im reign. Now Seraiah na quiet prince.
Jeremiah write for one book all di evil wey go come on Babylon, even all dis words wey dey written against Babylon.
Jeremiah talk to Seraiah, “When you come to Babylon, den see say you read all dis words,
and talk, ‘Di Lord, you don speak concerning dis place, to cut am off, so that none go remain inside am, neither man nor animal, but say e go be desolate forever.’
E go happen, when you don finish reading dis book, say you go tie stone to am, and cast am into di middle of di Euphrates.
Den you go talk, ‘Even so Babylon go sink, and go no rise again from di evil wey I go bring on her. Dem go dey weary.’” Di words of Jeremiah end here.
Zedekiah dey 21 years old when e begin to reign. E reign 11 years for Jerusalem. Im mother name na Hamutal, Jeremiah pikin of Libnah.
E do wetin dey evil for di eyes of di Lord, according to all wey Jehoiakim don do.
Because through di anger of di Lord e come to pass for Jerusalem and Judah, until e cast dem out from im presence. Zedekiah rebel against di king of Babylon.

E happen for di ninth year of im reign, for di tenth month, for di tenth day of di month, say Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon come, e and all im army, against Jerusalem, and encamp against am, and build siege walls against am all round.
So di city dey besieged until di eleventh year of King Zedekiah.
For di fourth month, for di ninth day of di month, di famine dey severe for di city, so that no bread dey for di people of di land.

Den di city dey broken into, and all di men of war flee, and go out of di city by night by di way of di gate between di two walls, wey dey by di king garden. (Now di Chaldeans dey against di city all round.) Dem go by di way of di Arabah.
But di army of di Chaldeans pursue di king, and overtake Zedekiah for di plains of Jericho. All im army dey scattered from am.
Den dem take di king, and bring am up to di king of Babylon to Riblah for di land of Hamath, and e pronounce judgment on am.
Di king of Babylon kill di sons of Zedekiah before im eyes. E kill also all di princes of Judah for Riblah.
Den e put out di eyes of Zedekiah, and di king of Babylon bind am in fetters, and carry am to Babylon, and put am for prison till di day of im death.

Now for di fifth month, for di tenth day of di month, wey be di nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon, Nebuzaradan di captain of di guard, wey serve di king of Babylon, come into Jerusalem.
E burn di house of di Lord, and di king house. All di houses of Jerusalem, even every great house, e burn with fire.
All di army of di Chaldeans wey dey with di captain of di guard break down all di walls of Jerusalem round about.

Den Nebuzaradan di captain of di guard carry away captive some of di poorest of di people, and di rest of di people wey remain for di city, and dem wey fall away, wey fall to di king of Babylon, and di rest of di multitude.
But Nebuzaradan di captain of di guard leave some of di poorest of di land for vinedressers and for farmers.
Di pillars of bronze wey dey di house of di Lord, and di bases, and di bronze sea wey dey di house of di Lord, di Chaldeans break in pieces, and carry all di bronze of dem to Babylon.
Di pots also, and di shovels, and di snuffers, and di basins, and di spoons, and all di vessels of bronze wey dem dey use for service, dem take away.
Di cups, and di fire pans, and di basins, and di pots, and di lampstands, and di spoons, and di bowls, wey be of gold, di gold, and wey be of silver, di silver, di captain of di guard take away.
Di two pillars, di one sea, and di twelve bronze bulls wey dey under di bases, wey King Solomon make for di house of di Lord. Di bronze of all dis vessels no dey weighed.
As for di pillars, di height of one pillar na 18 cubits, and thread of 12 cubits go measure am round. Im thickness na four fingers. E dey hollow.
One capital of bronze dey on am. Di height of one capital na five cubits, with network and pomegranates on di capital round about, all of bronze. Di second pillar get di same, with pomegranates.
Dey 96 pomegranates for di sides. All di pomegranates dey 100 upon di network round about.
Di captain of di guard take Seraiah di chief priest, and Zephaniah di second priest, and di three keepers of di threshold.

E take also out of di city one eunuch wey dey in charge of di men of war, and seven men of dem wey see di king face, wey dem find for di city, and di scribe of di captain of di army, wey mustered di people of di land, and 60 men of di people of di land, wey dem find for di middle of di city.
Nebuzaradan di captain of di guard take dem, and bring dem to di king of Babylon to Riblah.
Di king of Babylon strike dem, and put dem to death for Riblah for di land of Hamath. So Judah dey carried away captive out of im land.
Dis na di people wey Nebuchadnezzar carry away captive: for di seventh year, 3,023 Jews.
For di eighteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar, e carry away captive from Jerusalem 832 persons.
For di twenty-third year of Nebuchadnezzar, Nebuzaradan di captain of di guard carry away captive of di Jews 745 persons. All di persons na 4,600.

E happen for di 37th year of di captivity of Jehoiachin king of Judah, for di twelfth month, for di 25th day of di month, say Evil Merodach king of Babylon, for di first year of im reign, lift up di head of Jehoiachin king of Judah, and bring am out of prison.
E speak kindly to am, and set im throne above di throne of di kings wey dey with am for Babylon.
E change im prison garments, and e eat bread before am continually all di days of im life.
For im allowance, dem give am continual allowance from di king, each day im portion, until di day of im death, all di days of im life.
